title: 3 Stocks That Are Actually Cheap
creator: MarketBeat
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; guest interview with MarketBeat analyst Chris Markoch, hosted by Bridget.
summary: MarketBeat host Bridget and analyst Chris Markoch pitch three cheap, Thanksgiving-themed food stocks as 'sleep well at night' ballast against AI volatility, defining cheap as a PE below the S&P 500 average of about 20x and below the stock's own history. First, Smithfield Foods (SFD, BUY, first tracked): under $20, PE about 8.3x, roughly 6.5% yield on a $0.31 quarterly dividend. Packaged meats are strong (fifth straight year of $1bn operating profit) but the fresh-pork segment lost $89m last quarter as hog prices fell; the stock is down about 15% year to date and the dividend looks safe on $1.18bn of cash generated last quarter. Bridget added SFD to her paper-trading watch list. Second, McCormick (MKC, BUY, first tracked): about $47, PE about 9x, about 4% yield on $0.51 quarterly, a dividend aristocrat with 38 straight years of increases, down about 30% year to date on the planned Unilever food-business combination; low beta under 1. Third, Seneca Foods (SENEA, BUY, first tracked): about $37, PE about 10x, no dividend, up about 60% in 2026 but still about 14% below the analyst price target of $40-plus; LIFO accounting swings headline earnings, debt is coming down, and holiday promotions are a seasonal tailwind.
